title: Dimensional reduction for optical beams with thermal nonlocal nonlinearity
abstract: Nonlocal optical nonlinearities arising from the thermorefractive effect provide a long-range material response determined by heat diffusion and absorption. In graded-index media, this nonlocality fundamentally alters modal interactions, yet its accurate modeling remains computationally demanding when starting from the full spatial nonlinear Schrödinger equation. In this work, inspired by the nonpolynomial Schrödinger equation (NPSE) framework, we extend the dimensional reduction techniques to incorporate thermally mediated nonlocal nonlinearities. By coupling the optical field to an equation for the temperature-induced refractive index change, and employing a variational ansatz based on Laguerre--Gauss modes of the annular kind, of arbitrary azimuthal order, we derive explicit analytic expressions for the variational equations. The resulting effective model captures the dependence of the nonlinear interaction on mode order and degree of nonlocality, providing a tractable reduced description of the dynamics in thermal nonlocal media.
summary: This paper develops a method to simplify the complex dynamics of optical beams in thermally nonlinearly coupled media. By applying dimensional reduction techniques using Laguerre-Gauss mode ansatze, the authors derive an effective 1D model. This provides a computationally tractable framework for understanding how nonlocal thermal effects alter beam propagation compared to simpler local models.
main_problem: The work aims to extend dimensional reduction techniques, inspired by the nonpolynomial Schrödinger equation (NPSE), to model optical beams propagating in media exhibiting thermal nonlocal nonlinearity.
main_result: Explicit analytic expressions for variational equations are derived, yielding a tractable, reduced 1D description of beam dynamics that captures mode order and nonlocality dependence.
method: The authors employ a variational ansatz based on Laguerre–Gauss modes to reduce the full spatial nonlinear Schrödinger equation coupled to a screened Poisson heat equation into a set of coupled ordinary differential equations.
model_or_system: The system models optical beam propagation in a graded-index medium where the nonlinearity arises from the thermorefractive effect. The governing physics involves coupling the paraxial wave equation with a screened Poisson equation for temperature, which dictates the nonlocal refractive index change.
key_observables: Axial amplitude $|A(z)|^2$, transverse width $\sigma(z)$, and radial intensity profiles $|\Phi(r)|^2$.
important_parameters: Nonlocality length scale ($L_{	ext{eff}}$), linear losses coefficient ($\alpha_0$), GRIN potential strength ($\Omega$), and the nonlinear coupling constant ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include using the paraxial approximation, employing a variational ansatz based on annular Laguerre–Gauss modes, and approximating the heat diffusion equation with a screened Poisson-type model.
figures_summary: Figures compare radial intensity profiles $|\Phi(r)|^2$ between exact numerical solutions and the variational ansatz for various nonlocality strengths ($L_{	ext{eff}}$) and vortex orders. They also track the evolution of amplitude and width over propagation distance $z$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the full coupled system (NLSE + screened Poisson). It then details the variational reduction process, deriving effective Lagrangians for different components (local vs. nonlocal). Finally, it analyzes the resulting reduced equations by comparing predictions against known exact solutions and examining parameter dependence.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it tackles complex nonlinear wave propagation in structured media, providing analytical tools (variational reduction) where full numerical simulation of nonlocal effects is prohibitive.

The nonlinear pa- rameters are γ = −0.15, Leff = 40, α = 0.2, and Ω= 1.

Figure 4 shows the dynamical evolution of a vortex beam S = 1 propagating with losses set to α = 0.2 with strong thermal nonlocality Leff = 40. The correspon- dence between the reduced one-dimensional variational model (solid red lines) and the full two-dimensional split- step Fourier simulations (blue markers) is substantial.
